subject: tool:probe
value: TWO TOOLS, ONE FAILURE: a number reported against an UNNAMED or WRONG reference reads as a measurement of the thing the reader cares about. Both instances were measured this run and both are one-line reference errors, not algorithm errors. (1) PREFLIGHT vs GATE. `gdlmem.py propose-record --size` measured the record ON DISK while `stage_record_proposal` stamps `valid_from` and `recorded_at` BEFORE `_validate_record` applies the 16 KB attempt cap. The two stamps cost EXACTLY 67 bytes when both are absent (`, "recorded_at": "2026-09-04T02:09:23Z"` = 39, `, "valid_from": "2026-09-04"` = 28), which is the ~60-70 B a lane spent three trim cycles chasing. Demonstrated on a boundary record built to exactly the cap: authored 16384 B, the preflight said `over_by 0` / `within the 16384-byte attempt cap`, and the gate refused the same record `is 16451 bytes (cap 16384, OVER BY 67)`. A preflight that says UNDER where the gate says OVER is worse than no preflight -- it costs a full authoring round-trip -- so the preflight now runs the staging stamps itself and reports `staging_overhead_bytes` in the verdict. (2) TRANSITION vs BASELINE. probe's COUNT-PARITY banner is a CLASS statement about the function ('this function has just become eligible for a postprocessor class') computed against `last_insns`, i.e. whatever the previous probe left behind. Measured, attempt.CR_critterremovecolnodesub-the-two-pointer-hitnode-split-costs-one-instruction-or-folds-back.20260904.v1: a function that was T77/O77 at HEAD and throughout, one failed probe at T77/O78, and the next probe announced `COUNT-PARITY GAINED insns T77/O78 -> T77/O77` -- 'true only against probe (1)'s failed state ... The banner compares to the PREVIOUS PROBE, not to the commit, and reads like an achievement.' Run 49's `--discard` re-score closed ONE route to a stale previous state; it did not make the reference right. The banner now computes against `baseline_insns` (the clean-state count the first probe banks, which the first-baseline trap already requires), NAMES the reference in the line, reports an intermediate probe only as context, and emits `COUNT-PARITY HELD ... NOT a class change` where it used to claim a gain. THE GENERAL RULE: any tool line of the form `X -> Y` must print WHICH state Y is being compared against, and a preflight must run the gate's own serializer over the gate's own input. NEGATIVE SIDE HELD IN BOTH CASES: a genuine parity gain still announces itself (baseline T289/O290 -> T289/O289 on draw_power_meter, attempt.NC_draw-power-meter-pooled-base-buys-count-parity-and-the-tu-wide-pooling-claim-is-false.20260903.v1, and it survives an intermediate probe that also lost parity), and a comfortably sized record still reads as within the cap.
